cohort: The study included all women experiencing life-threatening conditions (either maternal near miss or maternal mortality) during pregnancy, childbirth, or within 42 days of termination of pregnancy, who presented to a tertiary care centre.
finding: The maternal near miss incidence ratio was 9.6 per 1000 live births, and the most common underlying causes were hypertensive disorders (48.42%) and anaemia (18.94%).
